Mikoyan MiG-29: Russian Aircraft Corporation MiG. The Mikoyan MiG-29 (Russian: Микоян МиГ-29; NATO reporting name: Fulcrum) is a twin-engine fighter aircraft designed in the Soviet Union.
Which company manufactures BAE Systems Hawk?
BAE Systems Hawk: Hawker Siddeley. The BAE Systems Hawk is a British single-engine, subsonic, jet-powered advanced trainer aircraft.
Who is credited with discovering Leo Minor?
Leo Minor: Johannes Hevelius. Leo Minor is a small and faint constellation in the northern celestial hemisphere.
Who is credited with discovering Graph theory?
Graph theory: Leonhard Euler. In mathematics and computer science, graph theory is the study of graphs, which are mathematical structures used to model pairwise relations between objects.
Who is credited with discovering Budesonide?
Budesonide: Ralph Brattsand. Budesonide, sold under the brand name Pulmicort, among others, is a steroid medication.
Who is credited with discovering Platinum?
Platinum: Julius Caesar Scaliger. Platinum is a chemical element; it has symbol Pt and atomic number 78.
This Swiss chemist discovered the structure of chitin in 1929 and decades later authored a memoir titled 'LSD: My Problem Child' — who was he?
Albert Hofmann (11 January 1906 - 29 April 2008) was a Swiss chemist known for being the first to synthesize, ingest, and learn of the psychedelic effects of lysergic acid diethylamide (LSD).

Usually a symptom of coronary artery disease caused by atherosclerosis narrowing the arteries, this chest pain or pressure gets its name from Latin words meaning 'to strangle' and 'chest' — name this condition?
Angina is chest pain or pressure, usually caused by insufficient blood flow to the heart muscle (myocardium).
This general medical term describes a joint disorder in which the smooth cartilage lining wears away, leaving bone to grind directly on bone during movement — what condition is it?
Arthritis is a general medical term used to describe a disorder in which the smooth cartilagenous layer that lines a joint is lost, resulting in bone grinding on bone during joint movement.
Grown for its edible taproot in red or golden varieties and closely related to Swiss chard, this vegetable's leaves are eaten too, sold simply as "greens" — which root vegetable?
Beetroot is the taproot portion of a Beta vulgaris subsp.
In service with the U.S. Air Force since 1955 — and flown by NASA until 2007 — this subsonic strategic bomber can haul 70,000 pounds of weapons nearly 8,800 miles without refueling. Which aircraft?
Boeing B-52 Stratofortress is an American nuclear-capable subsonic jet-powered strategic bomber.
This English-like, compiled programming language was designed for business use and remains widely used today to maintain legacy mainframe systems in banking and government — what language is it?
COBOL (Common Business-Oriented Language) is a compiled English-like computer programming language designed for business use.
This clouding of the eye's lens is responsible for nearly 40 percent of blindness cases worldwide, often causing halos around lights and trouble seeing at night — what condition is it?
Cataract is a cloudy area in the lens of the eye that impairs vision.
Most species of this loud insect superfamily emerge annually, but a few North American ones famously emerge en masse only once every several years. What insects are they?
Cicada are a superfamily, the Cicadoidea, of insects in the order Hemiptera (true bugs).

Serving as personal doctor to a superstar singer on the day of his 2009 death, this physician was later convicted of involuntary manslaughter over the misuse of a surgical anesthetic as a sleep aid — who is he?
Conrad Murray (born February 19, 1953) is a Grenadian-born American former physician convicted for his role in the death of American singer and dancer Michael Jackson.

He's the only person to have won BAFTAs in black-and-white, colour, high-definition, 3D and 4K — a broadcasting career that began way back in 1954 hosting Zoo Quest. Who is this English natural historian?
David Attenborough (born 8 May 1926) is an English broadcaster, natural historian, and writer.
This Penn professor's discoveries about modified nucleosides made the Pfizer and Moderna COVID-19 vaccines possible, earning him a share of the 2023 Nobel Prize in Medicine — who is he?
Drew Weissman (born September 7, 1959) is an American physician and immunologist known for his contributions to RNA biology.
This Italian-American physicist won the 1938 Nobel Prize, built the world's first artificial nuclear reactor (Chicago Pile-1), and is called the "architect of the nuclear age" — who was he?

Enrico Fermi (29 September 1901 - 28 November 1954) was an Italian-American physicist, renowned for being the creator of the world's first artificial nuclear reactor, the Chicago Pile-1, and a member of the Manhattan Project.
This mutual prodrug fuses amphetamine and theophylline into one molecule, marketed as a psychostimulant and better known today as a smuggled illicit street drug — what compound is it?
Fenethylline (BAN, USAN) or fenetylline (INN) is a codrug of amphetamine and theophylline and so a mutual prodrug of both.
Home to the supermassive black hole known as Sagittarius A*, this point roughly 26,000 light-years from Earth marks the barycenter around which the Milky Way rotates — what is it?
Galactic Center is the barycenter of the Milky Way and a corresponding point on the rotational axis of the galaxy.

This American computer scientist and Navy rear admiral devised the theory of machine-independent programming languages and used it to help create COBOL, after being one of the first programmers on the Harvard Mark I — who is she?
Grace Hopper (ne Murray; December 9, 1906 - January 1, 1992) was an American computer scientist, mathematician, and United States Navy rear admiral.

Producer of Japan's first major turn-based role-playing video game, this Dutch-born American entrepreneur also secured console distribution rights to a Russian puzzle game and resolved the licensing disputes that brought it to the Game Boy — who is he?
Henk Rogers is a Dutch-born American video game designer and entrepreneur.
Often confused with a benign tumor, this cell-proliferation process increases an organ's cell count rather than the size of each cell — which term?

Hyperplasia (from Ancient Greek (hupr) 'over' and (plsis) 'formation'), or hypergenesis, is an enlargement of an organ or tissue caused by an increase in the amount of tissue that results from cell proliferation.
Whose 1687 book Principia Mathematica achieved the first great unification in physics and established classical mechanics?
This American social psychologist built 'moral foundations theory' on the idea that our moral reasoning springs from innate gut feelings rather than logic — who is he?
Jonathan Haidt (HYTE; born October 19, 1963) is an American social psychologist and author.
Home to aromatic herbs like mint, oregano, and lavender as well as the seed crop chia, this family of mostly herbaceous flowering plants is commonly known as the mints or deadnettles — which family?

Lamiaceae is a family of flowering plants commonly known as mints, deadnettles, or sages. The mint family as a whole has a cosmopolitan distribution comprising about 236 genera and around 6,900 to 7,200 species.
Equal to one cubic decimetre, this metric unit of volume was originally a base unit of the French metric system and derives its name from an old French unit of weight. What unit is it?

Litre (Commonwealth spelling) or liter (American spelling) (SI symbols L and l, other symbol used:) is a metric unit of volume. It is equal to 1 cubic decimetre (dm3), 1000 cubic centimetres (cm3) or 0.001 cubic metres (m3).
With about 6,640 living species across 27 orders — rodents and bats leading the count — this class of vertebrates feeds its young on milk. What is it?
Mammal (from Latin mamma 'breast') is a vertebrate animal of the class Mammalia.
Home to a relativistic plasma jet stretching nearly 5,000 light-years from its core, this giant elliptical galaxy sits in the constellation Virgo — which galaxy is it?
Messier 87 (also known as Virgo A or NGC 4486, generally abbreviated to M87) is a supergiant elliptical galaxy in the constellation Virgo that contains several trillion stars.
This fast-growing, drought-resistant tree native to northern India earns nicknames like 'drumstick tree' and 'horseradish tree,' and its leaves and seed pods are eaten as vegetables. What is it?
Moringa oleifera is a short-lived, fast-growing, drought-resistant tree of the family Moringaceae, native to northern India and used extensively in South and Southeast Asia.

An English aeronautical engineer who wrote novels like On the Beach and A Town Like Alice, he adopted a pen name specifically so his employers at Vickers wouldn't think him 'not a serious person.' Who is he?
Nevil Shute (17 January 1899 - 12 January 1960) was an English novelist and aeronautical engineer who spent his later years in Australia.

Physicians in this medical specialty diagnose and surgically treat eye disorders — and can often spot signs of diseases elsewhere in the body just by examining a patient's eyes — what specialty is it?
Ophthalmology is the branch of medicine that deals with the diagnosis, treatment, and surgery of eye diseases and disorders.
This British theoretical physicist, one of the founders of quantum mechanics, coined the term 'quantum electrodynamics' and shared the 1933 Nobel Prize in Physics with Erwin Schrödinger — who is he?
Paul Dirac (dih-RAK; 8 August 1902 - 20 October 1984) was a British theoretical physicist who is considered to be one of the founders of quantum mechanics.
With a musty odor like freshly cut hay, this toxic colorless gas is the double acyl-chloride cousin of carbonic acid, and it saw grim use as a chemical weapon in World War I. Name the compound?
Phosgene is an organic chemical compound with the formula COCl2.
This spiny rodent actually comes in two unrelated varieties, an Old World family and a New World family, whose lookalike coats of keratin quills evolved independently — what animal is it?
Porcupine are large rodents with coats of sharp spines, or quills, that protect them against predators.

Picture benzene, but with one CH swapped for a nitrogen: this flammable, weakly alkaline liquid reeks of fish and underpins countless drugs and vitamins, churned out at 20,000 tons a year — what compound is it?
Pyridine is a basic heterocyclic organic compound with the chemical formula C5H5N.

An emeritus fellow of an Oxford college and the first-ever holder of a professorship for the public understanding of science, this British evolutionary biologist is also known as a prominent atheist author — who is he?
Richard Dawkins (born 26 March 1941) is a British evolutionary biologist, zoologist, science communicator, noted atheist, and author.

Created by Martin Odersky to address criticisms of Java, this statically typed tool blends object-oriented and functional styles, compiles to JVM bytecode, and can even transpile to JavaScript — which one?
Scala (programming language) is a strongly statically typed high-level general-purpose programming language that supports both object-oriented programming and functional programming.
This small, wingless, primitive insect takes its name from its silvery grey color and darting, fish-like movements — and its scientific name hints at a diet of sugars and starches. What is it?
Silverfish (Lepisma saccharinum) is a species of small, primitive, wingless insect in the order Zygentoma (formerly Thysanura).
This Polish-American Manhattan Project mathematician dreamed up the Monte Carlo method, the cellular automaton, and the design behind thermonuclear weapons — who was he?
Stanisław Ulam (13 April 1909 - 13 May 1984) was a Polish and, later an American mathematician who made important contributions in advancing the understanding of nuclear physics and computer science.
Its Latin species name vulgare simply means 'common,' yet this Asteraceae-family perennial turned invasive after spreading from Europe and Asia to Australia and the Americas — which plant?
Tansy (Tanacetum vulgare) is a perennial, herbaceous flowering plant in the genus Tanacetum in the family Asteraceae, native to temperate Europe and Asia.
Joining a tech giant in 1998 to run worldwide operations, this executive served as its COO before stepping up to CEO the day Steve Jobs resigned in 2011 — who is he?
Tim Cook (born November 1, 1960) is an American business executive who has served as the chief executive officer (CEO) of Apple since 2011.
A byproduct of purine breakdown normally found in urine, elevated blood levels of this heterocyclic compound can cause gout and kidney stones — what's the compound (C5H4N4O3)?
Uric acid is a heterocyclic compound of carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, and hydrogen with the formula C5H4N4O3.
Intermediate in size between the Greyhound and the Italian Greyhound, this gentle, minimal-shedding sighthound turns into a bundle of energy the moment it's outdoors — which breed?
Whippet is a British breed of sighthound. It closely resembles the Greyhound and the smaller Italian Greyhound, and is intermediate between them in size.

These ear-shaped sea snails wear a shell with a row of breathing holes and a pearly inside, and their flesh is prized as a delicacy worldwide — about 70 species, the biggest a foot long. What are they?
Abalone: Common name for a group of sea snails.
One of the world's few semiaquatic vipers, this venomous pit viper of the southeastern United States coils and displays its fangs when threatened — what is it?
A succulent from the Arabian Peninsula, this popular potted plant stores a soothing gel of acemannan in its leaves — alongside a toxic compound called aloin. What is it?
Aloe vera: Species of plant. It is widely distributed, and is considered an invasive species in many world regions.
This English mathematician earned a knighthood and the Abel Prize for proving Fermat's Last Theorem, a problem that fascinated him since childhood in Nigeria. Who is he?
Andrew Wiles: British mathematician who proved Fermat's Last Theorem.

Latin for 'worm-shaped,' this finger-like, blind-ended tube branches off the cecum and, though long considered vestigial, may actually serve as a reservoir for beneficial gut bacteria. What structure is this?
Appendix (anatomy): Tube attached to the intestine.
This ocean giant, recorded at up to 680 kg, has vanished from the Black Sea but still roams the Mediterranean and both sides of another major ocean — which fish?
Atlantic bluefin tuna: Species of fish. The Atlantic bluefin tuna (Thunnus thynnus) is a species of tuna in the family Scombridae.

Members of the family Ursidae walk flat on plantigrade paws tipped with five claws that can't retract — and though most eat meat, the giant panda among them is mostly herbivorous. What animal is this?
Made by combining phenol and acetone, this compound forms 65 to 70 percent of the world's polycarbonate plastics production — which chemical?
Bisphenol A: Chemical used in plastics, xenoestrogen.
Formerly called the Russian Wolfhound until 1936, this Russian sighthound breed was originally used for hunting wolves. What breed is it?
Named after the Greek word for butter via butyric acid, this colorless, highly flammable gas exists as two isomers and vaporizes quickly at room temperature — what alkane is it?
The largest living rodent, this semiaquatic South American grass-grazer lives in sociable herds of 10 to 20 — sometimes up to a hundred — near rivers and ponds; what is it?
A Turkish geologist honored by academies from the US to Russia to Serbia, he received the Gustav-Steinmann-Medaille, geology's top German prize. Who is he?
Celâl Şengör: Turkish scientist, geologist. Ali Mehmet Celâl Şengör (Turkish: [ˈali ˈmehmet ˈdʒeɫal ˈʃænɟœɾ]; born 24 March 1955) is a Turkish geologist.
Once common as the refrigerant "Freon," these carbon-chlorine-fluorine compounds were phased out under the Montreal Protocol for chewing through the ozone layer — what are they?

Medieval German miners cursed an ore that looked metal-rich but smelted into nothing useful, naming it after a mischievous goblin — yet for centuries its blue pigment tinted glass and jewelry. Which element, symbol Co, atomic number 27, earned that goblin's name?
Cobalt: Chemical element with atomic number 27 (Co)
Considered the most renowned Greek mathematician since antiquity, he advanced measure theory and the calculus of variations and even gave thermodynamics an axiomatic formulation — who is it?

Named after a mythological Greek youth transformed into a tree after killing his pet stag, this genus of evergreen conifers is found across warm temperate regions of the Northern Hemisphere — which genus?
Cupressus: Several genera of evergreen conifers.
This field statistically studies human populations — their size and makeup — through the interplay of births, deaths, and migration — what is it?
Demography: Study of human populations and their structures.
Descended from the African wild ass and domesticated some 5,000 to 7,000 years ago, which working equine still numbers over 40 million worldwide?
Donkey: Domesticated animal primarily used for transportation.
Belonging to the order Anguilliformes and comprising roughly 1,000 species, these ray-finned predators transform dramatically from larva to adult and mostly live in salt water — what are they?
This fungal genus growing on rye and other cereals produces alkaloids that cause a poisoning condition in humans and livestock who eat contaminated grain — which group of fungi?
Ergot: Fungi of the genus Claviceps. The most prominent member of this group is Claviceps purpurea (rye ergot fungus).

Its mating has never once been observed in the wild, and its five life stages were once mistaken for five separate species — this critically endangered fish is threatened by dams and overfishing. What is it?
European eel: Species of fish. The five stages of their development were originally thought to be different species.
Once tapped as a source of natural rubber, though no longer used commercially for that purpose, this houseplant native to South and Southeast Asia is nicknamed the 'rubber tree.' Which species?
Ficus elastica: Species of banyan tree.

One of the first management consultants, this American mechanical engineer wrote a 1909 book — later voted the most influential management book of the 20th century — and helped found industrial engineering. Who was he?
Frederick Winslow Taylor: American mechanical engineer (1856–1915)
This mathematician founded set theory and proved that there are more real numbers than natural numbers, revealing an infinity of infinities — who is he?
With DNA up to 99% identical to ours, this troop-dwelling great ape — led by a dominant 'silverback' — is the largest living primate on Earth — what is it?
Gorilla: Genus of large African apes.
First described in 1893 during a flu pandemic and mistakenly blamed as its cause, this Gram-negative bacterium causes pneumonia and meningitis mainly in infants — which bacterium?
Haemophilus influenzae: Species of bacterium. The bacteria are mesophilic and grow best at temperatures between 35 and 37 °C.

Famous for the ideas of "bounded rationality" and "satisficing," this remarkable scholar won both a Turing Award and a Nobel in Economics — bridging computer science, economics, and psychology. Who was he?
Herbert A. Simon: American academic and Nobel Laureate (1916–2001)

Found only in the Americas from Alaska to Tierra del Fuego, these roughly 375 species pull off rapid, maneuverable flight thanks to an exceptional metabolism — and their males flaunt the widest plumage diversity of any bird — what are they?
Named from an Ancient Greek word for 'intestinal obstruction,' this medical condition disrupts the gut's normal propulsive movement, whether from lost peristalsis or a physical blockage — what is it?
Ileus: Disruption to the propulsive ability of the intestine.
A self-taught rocketeer and practicing occultist, this co-founder of both JPL and Aerojet invented the first castable composite rocket propellant before dying young in 1952. Who was he?
This English mathematician dreamed up the cellular automaton known as the Game of Life and spent his later years at Princeton — who was he?
This German-Finnish internet entrepreneur founded the file-hosting service Megaupload before U.S. authorities seized it in 2012 — who is he?
This biennial vegetable in the onion family has an edible bundle of leaf sheaths sometimes colloquially called a 'stem' — what is it?
Leek: Vegetable in the onion family. A leek is a biennial vegetable, a cultivar of Allium ampeloprasum, the broadleaf wild leek (syn.
Named after both a biblical sea monster and the author of 'Moby-Dick,' this extinct predatory sperm whale roamed ancient oceans roughly 9 million years ago — which genus?
Livyatan: Extinct genus of sperm whale from the Miocene epoch.
Marketed by Apple since 2001 for its line of Mac computers, this proprietary operating system derives from OPENSTEP for Mach and FreeBSD. What kind of system is it?
macOS, previously OS X and originally Mac OS X, is a proprietary Unix operating system derived from OPENSTEP for Mach and FreeBSD, marketed and developed by Apple since 2001.
The heaviest members of the squirrel family, these ground-dwelling herbivores live in groups through the summer before disappearing underground to hibernate all winter — what are they?
Marmot: Genus of mammals (large ground squirrels)
This WWII German monoplane fighter formed the backbone of the Luftwaffe alongside the Focke-Wulf Fw 190, though Allied aircrew nicknamed it after its designer — which aircraft?

Messerschmitt Bf 109: German WWII fighter aircraft family. The Messerschmitt Bf 109 is a monoplane fighter aircraft that was designed and initially produced by the German aircraft manufacturer Bayerische Flugzeugwerke (BFW).

This Serbian polymath — mathematician, astronomer, civil engineer — explained Earth's long-term climate swings by tracking our planet's shifting position relative to the Sun, a theory of cycles that now bears his name. Who was he?
Milutin Milanković: Serbian scientist and professor (1879–1958)
Produced by glands throughout the body's linings — including the respiratory, digestive, and urogenital tracts — which slippery substance traps and destroys harmful bacteria and viruses?
Mucus: Secretion produced by mucous membranes.

The Navy paid his Purdue aeronautical-engineering tuition under the Holloway Plan, and he flew the Grumman F9F Panther off the USS Essex in the Korean War before his most famous flight of all — which Ohio-born aviator was he?
Named for the daring Doolittle airmen of World War II, this subsonic stealth flying wing is being built to replace the B-1 and B-2 by 2040 — which aircraft is it?
Northrop Grumman B-21 Raider: American stealth bomber aircraft.

Traditionally eaten whole in French cuisine, with diners often covering their heads with a napkin while doing so, this small Eurasian songbird's population crashed from overhunting despite EU protection — which bird?
Ortolan bunting: Species of bird in Eurasia.
Defined as the distance at which one astronomical unit subtends an angle of one arcsecond, this unit equals about 3.26 light-years — which unit?
Parsec: Unit of length in astronomy.
Smaller than 3 millimetres and caused by leaking capillaries, these tiny red or purple skin spots can be forensically significant when found around the eyes or neck — what are they called?
Petechia: Small red or purple blemish on the skin, eyes, etc. due to rupture of capillaries.

Cultivated for its edible nuts since prehistoric times and native to the Mediterranean and the Levant, this pine species has earned the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit — which species?
Pinus pinea: Species of pine tree. Pinus pinea, the Italian stone pine or Mediterranean stone pine, is a tree from the pine family, Pinaceae.
Stockpiled for radiation emergencies, this oral compound floods and shields the thyroid gland — and also treats hyperthyroidism and the skin infection sporotrichosis. Which compound is it?

Harvested from Plantago seeds mainly grown in northern India, this dietary fiber relieves both constipation and mild diarrhea, and can modestly lower cholesterol and blood pressure with regular use. What is it?
Psyllium: Plant used as a dietary fiber.
This genus of muroid rodents gives its scientific name to the common rat, though not every animal called a rat actually belongs to it — which genus?
Sold under the brand name Rituxan, this monoclonal antibody treats non-Hodgkin lymphoma, rheumatoid arthritis and several other autoimmune conditions via slow IV infusion — what is it?
Named after a 19th-century American veterinary surgeon, this genus of rod-shaped, flagella-covered bacteria includes over 2,650 serotypes divided among just two species — what is it?
Salmonella: Genus of bacteria. Salmonella is a genus of rod-shaped, (bacillus) Gram-negative bacteria of the family Enterobacteriaceae.
People with this anxiety disorder are fully capable of speech but fall silent in specific situations or around specific people, even when staying quiet brings shame or punishment — what is it called?
Selective mutism: Anxiety disorder blocking speech. Selective mutism usually co-exists with social anxiety disorder.
The only species in its genus, this cosmopolitan pelagic fish from the mackerel family can grow past a metre long and matters hugely to global fisheries — which species?
Skipjack tuna: Species of fish. The skipjack tuna (Katsuwonus pelamis) is a perciform fish in the tuna family, Scombridae, and is the only member of the genus Katsuwonus.

Once meaning a Christian life oriented toward the Holy Spirit, this concept broadened over centuries to describe a subjective sense of the sacred and 'the deepest values and meanings by which people live,' often apart from organized religion. What's the term?
NATO nicknamed this Soviet variable-sweep-wing tactical bomber 'Fencer'; it was the USSR's first plane with an integrated digital navigation-and-attack system — which aircraft is it?
Sukhoi Su-24: Family of Soviet strike aircraft.
The lone living family within its primate infraorder, these small Southeast Asian mammals favor forests thick with liana vines, which give them vertical support as they climb — which animal?
The body's primary muscle of respiration, this dome-shaped sheet separates the chest cavity from the abdomen and contracts to pull air into the lungs — what is it?
Thoracic diaphragm: Sheet of internal skeletal muscle.
Approved in the US in 1981, this sedating antidepressant from the SARI class racked up more than 24 million prescriptions in 2023, making it the fifth most common antidepressant — what is it?
Trazodone: Antidepressant medication. Trazodone is an antidepressant medication used to treat major depressive disorder, anxiety disorders, and insomnia.
Roughly 20 to 30 centimeters long in adults, this smooth-muscle tube carries urine from each kidney down to the bladder — what is it called?
Ureter: Tubes used in the urinary system in most animals.
Known as the 'true foxes,' animals in this genus are smaller and bushier-tailed than any wolf or jackal, with a signature dark triangular mask between the eyes — which genus?
Vulpes: Genus of true foxes. The members of this genus are colloquially referred to as true foxes, meaning they form a proper clade.
Made up of eight carpal bones and home to the carpal tunnel and the anatomical snuff box, this joint connects the hand to the forearm — which body part?
Wrist: Part of the arm between the lower arm and the hand.

Borat is the second of four films built around Baron Cohen's characters from Da Ali G Show and Ali G Indahouse.
